title: Humanoid-Gym: A Minimal Open Sim-to-Real Locomotion Loop
content_lines: Source: [arXiv:2404.05695v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05695v2). Implementation claims are restricted to the pinned official repository linked by the Chinese page.

> **Bottom line:** Humanoid-Gym's contribution is a reproducible path from GPU training through cross-simulator playback to real-robot deployment. The engineering value is configuration and interface alignment, not evidence that any policy trained with its defaults transfers safely to any humanoid.
## Engineering problem
Many locomotion papers omit the glue between training observations/actions and the hardware loop. Frame, joint-order, scaling, PD, decimation, and simulator differences can dominate the algorithm.
## Method

The project trains a command-conditioned locomotion policy, checks it in a second simulator, and deploys through a concrete robot interface. Reward terms, domain randomization, observation/action normalization, and configuration inheritance make the sim-to-real contract visible.

![Table 4: randomized parameters](../assets/humanoid-gym-2404.05695v2/table-4-parameters.jpg)
The ranges define the claimed robustness envelope and should not be copied without platform identification.
## Decisive evidence

The useful evidence chain is policy behavior in the training simulator, replay in another simulator, then real deployment. Agreement across these stages diagnoses contract errors before hardware exposure.
## Paper-to-implementation mapping

The pinned code contains robot/environment configuration, rewards, observations, actions, randomization, policy runner, simulator playback, and deployment entry points. These files form one coupled artifact; changing only the URDF is not a port.
## Limits and evidence boundary

The open stack does not identify arbitrary actuator dynamics or validate safety automatically. Nominal transfer evidence is platform-, terrain-, and command-specific. High-energy tests still require independent limits, supports, and emergency procedures.
## Bounded engineering takeaway
Use the repository as an executable contract template. Add an automated trace comparison for identical observations/actions across simulators before tuning more RL hyperparameters.
## Reproduction checklist

Lock commit, robot assets, joint order, frames, units, normalization, decimation, PD, reward, randomization, policy export, and deployment protocol. Compare state/action traces across simulators and report real frequency, latency, tracking, falls, and intervention count.
